implementation_boundary: This draft specifies intended source data and AI behavior. It does not claim that either party, trainer profile, dialogue, guide entry, or custom AI requirement has been implemented.

league_attrition.source_evidence: The Sidney, Phoebe, Glacia, and Drake room scripts return control after victory and contain no HealPlayerParty call.
league_attrition.manual_healing: The player can open the native menu and spend carried recovery, status, and PP items before walking into the next room.
league_attrition.design_consequence: Each battle is independently difficulty 10, but HP, status, PP, and inventory decisions also matter across the connected League gauntlet. The dossiers do not assume a free reset.

gimmick_policy.allowed: Exactly one Mega Evolution per battle.

competitive_research.method: Every compact index record was mechanically searched first. The most relevant complete records were then inspected set by set; roster-only event results were used only for high-level structure, never as invented exact sets.

glacia.query_definition: Doubles records matching snow, stall-offense, Toxic or Infestation clocks, or at least one of Mamoswine, Toxapex, Glalie, Chien-Pao, or Iron Bundle.

drake.query_definition: Singles records containing a relevant Dragon while also carrying at least one of setup, hazards, pivoting, or Choice pressure.

format_evidence: docs/verdant_doubles_manifest.json marks TRAINER_GLACIA as a six-member double.
EverGrandeCity_GlaciasRoom uses TRAINER_GLACIA for the first League clear.
GLACIA.identity: Black-ice detonation and a venom clock: Glacia presents apparent stall beside an immediate Mega Glalie self-destruct threat, then changes into raw Sword of Ruin and Quark Drive offense without ever hiding behind Aurora Veil.
GLACIA.primary_player_question: Can the player scout or deny Mega Glalie's detonation while preventing Toxapex from trapping and poisoning the answer that must survive for Glacia's fast back line?
GLACIA.primary_mode: Mega Glalie and Toxapex open together. Refrigerate Double-Edge or Explosion creates immediate physical pressure while Baneful Bunker, Infestation, Toxic, and Wide Guard turn passive or overprotective play into a clock.
GLACIA.secondary_mode: Chien-Pao, Choice Scarf Chandelure, Focus Sash Mamoswine, and Booster Energy Iron Bundle form a no-dedicated-speed-control offense. Sword of Ruin, priority, two pivots, Fire coverage, and mixed damage force the player to win positions rather than simply reverse Tailwind or Trick Room.

intentional_opening.visible_problem: Glalie can attack normally, Protect, or spend itself on Refrigerate Explosion; Toxapex can protect itself, trap one target, poison, or block spread attacks.
intentional_opening.not_forced: The custom AI should strongly recognize the safe detonation opportunity but must not force Explosion when Double-Edge or preservation is better.

GLACIA.first_loss_lesson: Do not treat Toxapex as harmless support or assume Glalie must explode immediately. Scout the detonation, deny the trap or Toxic clock, and preserve a speed-control or priority answer for Chien-Pao and Iron Bundle.
intentional_weaknesses: The team has no snow setter, Aurora Veil, Tailwind, Trick Room, or redirection. Its speed can be reversed or reduced directly.
Taunt, Encore, Substitute, Misty Terrain, Safeguard, poison immunity, and prompt switching can make Toxapex spend turns without progress.
Mega Glalie is an Ice/Rock attacker with common Fighting, Steel, Rock, Water, Grass, and priority vulnerabilities; Explosion also permanently spends a full party slot.
Sword of Ruin lowers the Defense of Chien-Pao's own partner as well as the player's Pokemon, so physical counterpressure can exploit the supposedly offensive board.
Chandelure is Choice-locked and can be punished after Trick or a resisted attack; Mamoswine's Focus Sash can be broken by hazards, weather, or multihit damage.
counterplay_classes: Protect, Ghost immunity, resist switching, Fake Out, or focused priority to scout or stop Mega Glalie's detonation turn.
Taunt, Encore, Substitute, status prevention, poison immunity, trapping denial, or fast focus fire against Toxapex.
Icy Wind, Electroweb, paralysis, Trick Room, priority, Choice Scarf users, or raw faster threats against the no-setter fast mode.
Fighting, Steel, Fire, Rock, and Water pressure distributed across the Ice attackers, while Ground or Dark pressure checks Toxapex and Chandelure differently.
Knock Off, Trick, hazards, multihit moves, and exploiting Chandelure's Choice lock to dismantle the team's item-dependent seams.
GLACIA.difficulty_rationale: Six optimized Pokemon sit two to five levels over the cap. The opening combines a credible double-KO threat with a trapping/status clock, while the reserves include a major Ice legendary, two priority users, a Choice Scarf Fire immunity, and a Booster Energy speed apex. Broad counterplay exists, but a blind loss is expected because preserving the wrong answer for the wrong mode is costly.

manual_healing_attrition.before_battle: Glacia is the third League member. The player enters after Phoebe with no automatic restoration, but can spend carried items before initiating Glacia.
manual_healing_attrition.during_battle: Infestation, Toxic, repeated switching, Wide Guard pressure, and Glalie's explosive damage are intended to consume HP, status cures, and positioning resources even in a win.
manual_healing_attrition.after_battle: Control returns in Glacia's room and Hall 3. The player may manually heal before Drake, so the design taxes inventory without pretending healing is impossible.

custom_ai_requirements.requirement: Reward Refrigerate Explosion only when Toxapex or the current ally has selected protection, is immune, or the expected two-target payoff justifies losing Glalie; otherwise prefer Double-Edge, Ice Shard, Protect, or preservation.

Select Infestation and Toxic against a target that can actually be trapped and poisoned, avoid redundant clocks, recognize Baneful Bunker as the safe Explosion partner action, and use Wide Guard only against credible spread pressure.
Permit Toxapex to switch for Regenerator when the clock is established or its board role is exhausted, without abandoning an active trap at random.
Exploit Chandelure's Choice Scarf and Trick, and recognize that Sword of Ruin exposes Chien-Pao's partner as well as opposing Pokemon.

selected_references.evidence: Exact public team sheet; Wolfe Glick, 3rd at 2026 NAIC.
selected_references.decision: selected architecture and two exact roles
selected_references.adaptation: Preserve the Toxapex Infestation/Toxic/Wide Guard clock, Mamoswine pressure, and primary-clock/secondary-burst philosophy. Replace Charizard-Y sun, Sneasler, Hydreigon, and Incineroar with Glacia-specific Mega detonation, Sword of Ruin, Fire immunity, and Booster Energy pressure.
The reproducible Glalie Explosion set establishes the detonation role. Verdant upgrades it to the one Mega slot and removes the unrelated sand, sleep, and setup shell.
Life Orb Sword of Ruin, Icicle Crash, Sucker Punch, and Protect are retained; legal Sacred Sword replaces Throat Chop to break Steel and Ice answers.

selected_references.decision: selected Iron Bundle item and three-move shell
selected_references.adaptation: Booster Energy, Freeze-Dry, Hydro Pump, and Protect are retained. Encore is not present in Verdant's current Iron Bundle learnset, so legal Flip Turn replaces it.
Choice Scarf Flash Fire, Heat Wave, and Trick supply Fire and Steel counterpressure without adding weather or another setup mode.

The world champion roster demonstrates that positioning, priority, redirection, and Sword of Ruin can define difficulty without Tailwind or Trick Room. Glacia uses that anti-formula principle, not the roster.

rejected_references.reason: Ninetales-Alola, Aurora Veil, Icy Wind, and protected setup recreate Glacia's current generic screen-setter structure.
Aurora Veil into multiple setup recipients is strategically valid but duplicates a campaign pattern and does not produce a radically different Glacia.
Abomasnow Light Clay plus screen and speed-control support repeats the exact old Glacia spine.
Charizard-Y sun and three non-cold support species would make Glacia a costume placed on Wolfe's team rather than a native League identity.

Explicitly state that no snow or screen is coming.

format_evidence: docs/verdant_doubles_manifest.json deliberately marks TRAINER_DRAKE as a six-member single.
Drake's current native intro explicitly announces a singles duel.
The format shift follows three doubles League members and creates a legitimate concentration and resource-preservation test rather than a weaker version of their battles.
DRAKE.identity: The six-dragon preservation duel: early hazards and two visible Choice locks force exact switching decisions, anti-Fairy lures punish autopilot, Mega Dragonite attacks from the special side, and Zygarde closes with the only setup clock.
DRAKE.primary_player_question: Can the player preserve the correct Ice, Fairy, status, or Unaware answer through Stealth Rock, two Choice-locked lures, and mixed damage long enough to stop both Mega Dragonite and the final Power Construct Zygarde?
DRAKE.primary_mode: Rough Skin Rocky Helmet Garchomp establishes Stealth Rock and phazes greed; Choice Band Dragapult and Choice Scarf Hydreigon then force fast physical and special trades while pivoting out of bad locks.
DRAKE.secondary_mode: Assault Vest Adaptability Dragalge punishes the Fairy answer, special Mega Dragonite breaks the physical wall the opening invites, and Leftovers Power Construct Zygarde is the one deliberate setup-and-rest endgame.

intentional_opening.visible_problem: Stealth Rock makes every later preservation switch cost HP, while Dragon Tail prevents a free opening setup and Rocky Helmet plus Rough Skin punishes careless contact.
intentional_opening.not_forced: First-turn hazard preference should remain conditional on Garchomp surviving and the matchup; immediate Earthquake, Fire Blast, Dragon Tail, or switching must remain legal decisions.

DRAKE.first_loss_lesson: Record which attackers are Choice-locked, scout the anti-Fairy Flash Cannon and Sludge Bomb lures, and stop spending the dedicated Zygarde answer merely to win an earlier trade. Break Multiscale before trying to burst Mega Dragonite.
intentional_weaknesses: Every team member is a Dragon. Ice and Fairy offense remain structurally excellent once Dragalge, Flash Cannon Hydreigon, and Fire Blast lures are identified.
Dragapult and Hydreigon are Choice-locked; Protect, immunity switching, Disable, Encore, Trick, and prediction can convert their speed into free turns.
The roster has no cleric, hazard removal, screen, weather, terrain, priority support, or second setup sweeper.
Mega Dragonite's Multiscale is broken by Stealth Rock, status, weather chip, or any preliminary damage, and its special set can be answered by dedicated special bulk.

Zygarde deliberately uses legal Earthquake rather than unsupported Thousand Arrows, so Flying types, Levitate, Air Balloon, phazing, Haze, Unaware, Encore, Trick, and Ice attacks provide real endgame counterplay.
counterplay_classes: Hazard denial or removal, Magic Bounce, Taunt, and heavy immediate pressure against lead Garchomp.
Fairy and Ice offense combined with careful scouting of Hydreigon's Flash Cannon, Dragalge's Poison STAB, and Fire coverage.
Protect, immunity switching, Disable, Encore, item removal, or Trick to exploit Choice Band Dragapult and Choice Scarf Hydreigon.
Burn, Intimidate, Reflect, physical walls, and Rocky Helmet against Dragapult, Garchomp, and Zygarde; special walls against Hydreigon, Dragalge, and Mega Dragonite.
Haze, Clear Smog, Unaware, phazing, Encore, Taunt, Trick, sleep denial, and strong Ice pressure against the final Coil/Rest Zygarde.
Chip damage, hazards, status, priority, or a sacrificial weak hit to break Mega Dragonite's Multiscale before the decisive attack.
DRAKE.difficulty_rationale: The six Pokemon sit two to six levels over the cap and cover physical, special, fast, bulky, pivoting, lure, Mega, and legendary endgame roles without adding a second gimmick. Difficulty comes from irreversible preservation mistakes: Stealth Rock taxes correction, the two Choice users punish the wrong immunity, Dragalge removes the easy Fairy shortcut, Mega Dragonite reverses the expected defensive category, and Zygarde demands one surviving endgame plan.

manual_healing_attrition.before_battle: Drake is the fourth Elite Four member. The player enters after Glacia with no automatic restoration but can spend carried healing, status, and PP items in Glacia's room and Hall 3.
manual_healing_attrition.during_battle: Stealth Rock and forced switching deliberately convert party depth into HP attrition. Rest Zygarde can tax PP, but it has no evasion or infinite recovery loop and remains vulnerable to multiple broad denial classes.
manual_healing_attrition.after_battle: Control returns in Drake's room and Hall 4. The player may manually restore before entering Wallace's forced Champion approach; the dossier does not assume a free heal.

mega_audit.mapping_evidence: src/data/pokemon/evolution.h maps SPECIES_DRAGONITE plus ITEM_DRAGONINITE to SPECIES_DRAGONITE_MEGA; the Mega form exists with 700 BST and Multiscale.

custom_ai_requirements.requirement: Prefer Stealth Rock on global turn zero only when Garchomp survives and the hazard has value; prefer Dragon Tail against a credible setup state or a switch worth taxing, not as blind low-accuracy damage.
Track Dragapult's Band and Hydreigon's Scarf locks, use U-turn to escape losing locks, and switch rather than repeatedly choose an immune or heavily resisted target.
Activate Mega Dragonite as the one Mega, value Roost when it can restore a meaningful Multiscale threshold, and recognize its special rather than physical damage role.

Use Coil only in a safe endgame, Rest at an HP threshold that gains real value, Sleep Talk while asleep, and avoid switching away a viable sleeping Power Construct closer without a concrete matchup reason.

selected_references.evidence: Official 2025 World Champion roster indexed from public event results.
selected_references.adaptation: Giovanni's fast offense into a slower Ursaluna/Lunala mode inspires Drake's fast Choice pressure into a slow Zygarde close. No doubles support role or exact restricted roster is copied.

selected_references.decision: selected Dragapult and Garchomp offensive precedent
selected_references.adaptation: The published sample proves the pair can divide fast Ghost/Dragon pressure and Ground pressure. Drake rejects its Aurora Veil and multiple setup recipients, using hazards, phazing, and Choice pressure instead.

selected_references.decision: selected exact Choice Band Dragapult shell
selected_references.adaptation: Dragon Darts, Dragon Claw, Phantom Force, and U-turn transfer cleanly into singles and provide an exploitable lock instead of another setup clock.
Dark Pulse, Flash Cannon, and Fire coverage establish Hydreigon as a Fairy and Steel lure. Verdant uses Choice Scarf, Draco Meteor, and U-turn to make its commitment readable.
Dragon and Poison special pressure plus Focus Blast become Drake's deliberate anti-Fairy sponge, with Assault Vest replacing passive Black Sludge.

Roost and Multiscale are retained, but Verdant's Champions Mega has 145 Special Attack, so Drake deliberately reverses the expected physical Dragonite answer with Draco Meteor, Hurricane, and Fire Blast.

selected_references.decision: selected Zygarde endgame concept with legality correction
selected_references.adaptation: Power Construct and one setup endgame are retained. Unsupported Thousand Arrows and the second Dragon Dance clock are rejected in favor of fully source-legal Earthquake, Coil, Rest, and Sleep Talk.

rejected_references.reason: The published DD Triple team proves layered setup can work, but three setup clocks would repeat Verdant's earlier overstuffing problem and make Drake less learnable.
TerrakChomp hyper offense supplies useful pressure precedent, but another physical Dragon Dance Dragonite would duplicate Zygarde's endgame and waste the new Mega Dragonite's special-stat identity.
Salamence plus Palkia is a viable Dragon shell, but the roster's unrelated hazard pieces and repeated Thunder Wave do not produce a bespoke final Elite Four duel.

Dialga, Zygarde, Reshiram, Naganadel, Rayquaza, and Mega Salamence stack five legendary-scale Pokemon and three setup clocks without a clear singles sequence. Raw BST does not substitute for a preservation puzzle.

static_validation_summary.species: All twelve base species and both intended Mega forms exist in the current engine data.
static_validation_summary.items: All twelve held-item constants exist. Exactly one Mega Stone appears per dossier.
static_validation_summary.abilities: Every requested ability exists in the recorded slot: Refrigerate 0, Regenerator 2, Sword of Ruin 0, Flash Fire 0, Thick Fat 2, Quark Drive 0, Rough Skin 2, Clear Body 0, Levitate 0, Adaptability 2, Multiscale 2, and Power Construct 0.
static_validation_summary.moves: Every move resolves through current level, TM/HM, tutor, imported Gen 9, or family egg-move data. The draft explicitly avoids Iron Bundle Encore and Zygarde Thousand Arrows because they are absent from the current player-facing learnset sources.
static_validation_summary.formats: Glacia remains a native double and Drake remains a deliberate native single.
static_validation_summary.cap: Both are specified relative to the source-backed cap of 80.
static_validation_summary.healing: No automatic League-room healing was found; manual item healing is incorporated into both dossiers.
static_validation_summary.runtime_claim: No runtime claim is made until source implementation, compilation, and representative playtesting are complete.
